question.text: In the context of financial markets, what is the key difference between a depository and a custodian?

answer.text: A depository can effect transfer of beneficial ownership while a custodian cannot
A custodian can effect transfer of beneficial ownership while a depository cannot
A depository only deals with equity shares while a custodian deals with all securities
There is no difference as both perform identical functions

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the NISM-III-C workbook, a depository holds dematerialised securities for beneficial owners and has the right to effect transfer of beneficial ownership. A custodian provides safekeeping, trade settlement, benefit collection and reporting services for institutional investors but cannot effect a transfer of beneficial ownership. The Trap: Option B reverses the distinction. Option C is wrong because the workbook treats depositories as holding dematerialised securities of all types, not only equity. Note: Source — NISM-Series-III-C workbook (January 2026), page 13 (depositories holding dematerialised securities for beneficial owners) and page 15 (transfer-of-beneficial-ownership distinction between depository and custodian).
